Caitlin Clark Foundation Receives $22,000 Grant from Gainbridge Assists, Highlighting Support for Girls' Sports

02 Nov 2026, 04:31 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

3 min read

Introduction

The Caitlin Clark Foundation, the charitable arm of Indiana Fever WNBA star Caitlin Clark, has been awarded a special $22,000 grant through the 2025 Gainbridge Assists programme. The announcement, made on September 4, 2025, places the foundation among 32 organisations receiving funding to expand opportunities for girls and women in sport and education.

Grant Details

  • Programme: Gainbridge Assists (third year) – a partnership between Gainbridge, Parity and the Women’s Sports Foundation.
  • Total funding announced: $222,000 for 32 recipients across 21 U.S. states.
  • Standard grant: $5,000 per organisation for a specific event or project.
  • Special grants: $22,000 to the Caitlin Clark Foundation; $50,000 to the Turnstone Center for Children and Adults with Disabilities.
  • Focus areas for Clark’s grant: Education, nutrition and sports – the three pillars the foundation cites as central to its mission.

Comments from Stakeholders

  • Mike Nichols, Group 1001’s chief of sponsorship strategy, said in the press release: “*Gainbridge Assists continues to grow in reach and resonance levels, supporting changemakers who are breaking down barriers and fostering participation and leadership.*” He added that the initiative is “*about investing in equity, access, and the belief that every girl deserves a shot at her dreams.*”
  • Billie Jean King, tennis legend and founder of the Women’s Sports Foundation, praised the cohort: “*This is an opportunity for each of the organizations to make a huge difference for the next generation of girls and women.*”
  • Caitlin Clark previously described the foundation’s purpose during a 2024 partnership announcement: “*The Caitlin Clark Foundation aims to improve the lives of youth through three pillars – education, nutrition, and sports.*” The 2025 grant is a repeat of that earlier support.

Practical Implications

  • Programmatic use: The $22,000 can fund a community‑based event, scholarship, nutrition workshop, or sports clinic that aligns with the foundation’s three‑pillar model.
  • Geographic reach: While the programme covers 21 states, the foundation can choose any location where it already operates, expanding its impact beyond Indiana.
  • Visibility: Association with high‑profile figures such as Billie Jean King and a national corporate sponsor may attract additional donors and volunteers.
  • Accountability: Recipients are expected to report on how the funds were spent and the outcomes achieved, providing a transparent trail for future grant cycles.

How to Verify the Announcement

  1. Official press release – Gainbridge, Parity and the Women’s Sports Foundation posted a joint announcement on their websites on September 4, 2025. The release lists all 32 grant recipients and the amounts awarded.
  2. Times of India article – The news story (URL provided below) reproduces the key details and includes quotes from the involved parties.
  3. Foundation’s website/social media – The Caitlin Clark Foundation typically posts grant acknowledgments and project updates; a post dated early September 2025 should confirm receipt of the $22,000.
  4. Public filings – As a registered nonprofit, the foundation’s Form 990 (available through Guidestar or the IRS) will later reflect the grant under “contributions received.”

Conclusion

The special $22,000 grant underscores the growing ecosystem of corporate‑philanthropic programmes that target gender equity in sport. By channeling resources into education, nutrition and athletic participation, the Caitlin Clark Foundation can create measurable benefits for girls who might otherwise lack access to such opportunities. Stakeholders and the public can track the grant’s impact through the foundation’s reporting mechanisms and the transparent documentation provided by Gainbridge Assists.
